lines.text: Do you know how a message pops up on your phone the instant it's sent? Your phone isn't constantly asking for news.
Checking every few seconds would drain your battery. So instead, your phone keeps one quiet connection open, all the time.
On an iPhone it goes to Apple's push servers, on Android to Google's. Every app shares that one line.
When someone messages you, their app's server sends a tiny note to Apple or Google, who pass it down that open line.
The note wakes the app, which shows it, or fetches the rest of the message.
The whole trip usually takes about a second, even from the other side of the world.
Orbi works the same way for files. Every open Orbi screen joins a live room for its area. A new file sends only a tiny note, and nearby screens show it within about a second.
